emmenager.q1: How much time do you already spend together each week?
emmenager.q1a: We sleep together almost every night, we practically live together already.
emmenager.q1b: 3-4 nights a week. We've found our rhythm.
emmenager.q1c: 1-2 times a week. We mostly see each other on weekends.
emmenager.q1d: Less than that. We haven't really tested daily life together yet.
emmenager.q2: Have you ever spent more than 2 consecutive weeks together (vacation, trip, lockdown)?
emmenager.q2a: Yes, and it went great. We actually enjoyed it.
emmenager.q2b: Yes, it was good but with a few tense moments.
emmenager.q2c: Yes, and it was rough. We needed breaks.
emmenager.q2d: No, never. We haven't had the chance yet.
emmenager.q3: Is your definition of "tidy" and "clean" the same?
emmenager.q3a: Pretty much, yes. We have similar standards.
emmenager.q3b: Not exactly, but we know how to compromise on that.
emmenager.q3c: Not at all. One of us is a neat freak, the other lives in chaos.
emmenager.q4: How do you handle the other person's need for alone time?
emmenager.q4a: We respect it naturally. If one needs space, the other understands without taking it personally.
emmenager.q4b: We manage, but it takes some effort. One of us can take it a bit personally.
emmenager.q4c: It's a source of conflict. Asking for time alone is seen as a problem.
emmenager.q5: Financially, how do you plan to split expenses?
emmenager.q5a: We've discussed it clearly: rent, groceries, bills, everything is laid out.
emmenager.q5b: We have a general idea, but the details are still fuzzy.
emmenager.q5c: We haven't talked about it at all.
emmenager.q6: Has either of you lived with a roommate or partner before?
emmenager.q6a: Yes, both of us. We know what it's like to share a space.
emmenager.q6b: One of us has, the other hasn't.
emmenager.q6c: Neither of us. We're starting from scratch on this one.
emmenager.q7: What happens when one of you is in a bad mood?
emmenager.q7a: We give each other space. We talk about it when things calm down.
emmenager.q7b: It creates some tension, but it doesn't escalate.
emmenager.q7c: It poisons everything. If one is upset, it's a cold war for everyone.
emmenager.q8: Do you agree on the idea of getting a pet?
emmenager.q8a: Yes, we're on the same page (whether we want one or not).
emmenager.q8b: Not really, but it's not a hot topic right now.
emmenager.q8c: It's a real point of disagreement between us.
emmenager.q9: Are your daily routines compatible (schedules, sleep, evenings)?
emmenager.q9a: Yes, we generally live on the same schedule.
emmenager.q9b: There are some gaps, but nothing unmanageable.
emmenager.q9c: One's an early bird, the other's a night owl. That's going to clash.
emmenager.q10: How would you react if the other invited friends over without asking?
emmenager.q10a: No problem at all, it's our place.
emmenager.q10b: I'd prefer a heads-up, but I can adapt.
emmenager.q10c: It would really bother me. I need to control my space.
emmenager.q11: Have you talked about decorating and setting up the place?
emmenager.q11a: Yes, and we have compatible tastes (or at least the ability to compromise).
emmenager.q11b: Vaguely. We'll figure it out when we get there.
emmenager.q11c: Our tastes are polar opposites and neither of us wants to budge.
emmenager.q12: How do you handle chores when you're together?
emmenager.q12a: We split things naturally, without anyone having to ask.
emmenager.q12b: One does a bit more, but we talk about it.
emmenager.q12c: One does everything, the other waits to be told.
emmenager.q13: What's your relationship with noise at home (music, TV, speakerphone)?
emmenager.q13a: We have pretty much the same noise habits.
emmenager.q13b: There are differences, but we work it out (headphones, separate rooms).
emmenager.q13c: It's a point of friction. One needs silence, the other lives with constant noise.
emmenager.q14: Are you ready to give up some of your personal space?
emmenager.q14a: Yes, that's the deal. And we've planned how to keep a corner for each of us.
emmenager.q14b: In theory yes, but I'll admit it makes me a bit anxious.
emmenager.q14c: I'm not sure I want to share my space 24/7.
emmenager.q15: How does it go when you cook together (or each on your own)?
emmenager.q15a: We love cooking together. Or we each do our own thing and it flows.
emmenager.q15b: It's fine, as long as we're not stepping on each other's toes in the kitchen.
emmenager.q15c: The kitchen is a minefield. We don't have the same food habits or relationship with cooking.
emmenager.q16: If one of you is going through a tough time (stress, unemployment, low mood), how does the other react?
emmenager.q16a: They're present and patient, without smothering. We know how to support each other.
emmenager.q16b: We do our best, but it's not always easy to handle.
emmenager.q16c: It throws the whole relationship off. We don't handle each other's rough patches well.
emmenager.q17: Do you have a clear idea of the rent + bills budget you can afford together?
emmenager.q17a: Yes, we've done the math. We know what we can put in.
emmenager.q17b: We have a rough range but haven't nailed down the exact numbers.
emmenager.q17c: No idea. We haven't discussed finances in detail.
emmenager.q18: What happens if one of you wants to go out and the other wants to stay in?
emmenager.q18a: No problem. Each does their own thing, no guilt-tripping.
emmenager.q18b: It happens and sometimes creates a little tension, but nothing serious.
emmenager.q18c: One feels abandoned or the other feels held back. It's complicated.
emmenager.q19: Your respective families: what level of intrusion do you expect?
emmenager.q19a: Our families respect our space. We handle it well.
emmenager.q19b: There are one or two potential invaders, but we know how to set boundaries.
emmenager.q19c: The in-laws are going to show up all the time, and it's already a source of stress.
emmenager.q20: Be honest: why do you want to move in together?
emmenager.q20a: Because we're happy together, we want to build something, and the timing is right.
emmenager.q20b: Mostly for practical reasons (finances, distance, lease ending). The desire is there too, but it's not the main driver.
emmenager.q20c: Because we've been together for X amount of time and "it's the next logical step."
emmenager.r1_d: Let's be honest: your answers show that you don't yet have the foundation to live under the same roof. This doesn't question your feelings (you can love each other deeply and still not be ready to share a fridge). But the practical topics haven't been addressed enough, and there are too many gaps.
emmenager.r1_a: Moving in now could turn your love story into a tense roommate situation. Take the time to build your relationship at its own pace. If you're wondering whether your relationship is healthy, that might be where to start before thinking about a shared apartment.
emmenager.r2_d: This score doesn't say "you're not meant to live together." It says "not right now, not like this." Your answers reveal significant gaps: about lifestyle, money, managing shared space, or mutual expectations.
emmenager.r2_a: Moving in with these unresolved friction points means putting your relationship under unnecessary pressure. Keep seeing each other, go on vacation together, try extended weekends. And come back to take this test in 3-4 months.
emmenager.r3_t: Almost ready, but a few more questions to sort out
emmenager.r3_d: The foundation is there. So is the desire. But there are still some gray areas between you. Maybe the budget, maybe the chore split, maybe noise levels or alone time.
emmenager.r3_a: These topics can be ignored as long as you don't live together. Once you do, they blow up within 3 weeks. Grab a bottle of wine one evening and put everything on the table. An awkward conversation now beats a blowup over the dishes in 2 months.
emmenager.r4_d: Your answers show two people who have already tested daily life together and know what to expect. You've talked about money, chores, and the need for personal space. It's not glamorous, but that's exactly what makes a move-in go well.
emmenager.r4_a: The biggest risk for you? Idealizing life together a bit too much and forgetting that even the strongest couples have days where they think "I want to be alone in my own apartment." Keep your solo hobbies, keep your friends, keep a corner that's just yours in the apartment.
emmenager.gap_low_d: Your visions of life together are similar. That's a very positive sign. Daily life always has surprises in store, but you're starting with the same expectations.
emmenager.gap_mid_d: One of you is clearly more ready (or more enthusiastic) than the other. That's not a problem in itself, but you need to talk about it. Look at the questions where your answers differ the most: that's where the real conversations are hiding.
emmenager.gap_high_d: You don't see moving in together the same way at all. One is charging ahead, the other is holding back (or isn't aware of the implications). Before signing a lease, sit down and talk. Really. A gap this big deserves an honest discussion, and maybe a bit more time.
